title: Goodnight Stories | The Flowers Never Given
subtitle: The roses are yours. So am I.
body: **NOTE:** The author has cured her brief broken-heart syndrome, so this heartbreak story, previously shut away in a little dark room, has been let out too. **NOTE 2:** May I be the moonlight in your room, lending you light when you are bored. **NOTE 3:** This is a story I wrote in 2021 for someone I liked then. Time has passed; suddenly I feel that both characters in this story are myself. That is rather interesting too. 01 Lin, Please stop being angry with me, will you? I didn’t mean to shout at you that day. I really didn’t. I was too nervous. I’m afraid of dying, but even more afraid of losing you. I never really cared about that Prometheus Project. But you said you wanted to protect the spark of humanity, so I came along. I hadn’t realized how important this was to you. I’m sorry. Next time I operate the escort ship, I’ll be careful, careful, and more careful. With the mothership between us, I can only try to imagine where you are. Please stop ignoring me, will you? I know you’re only angry with me. Talk to me, please? Flying escort ship Beta alone is so boring. Leng, who loves you 02 Lin, It’s been so long, and you still won’t talk to me? Can you stop making such a fuss over nothing? I’ve apologized, and the spark of Prometheus is safe. What more do you want! I know you received my letter aboard escort ship Alpha. Why haven’t you replied after all this time! You were always like this before. Every time we argued, you’d stop talking to me. I hate it most when you give me the silent treatment. After every argument, I have to plead and plead before I can coax you out of it. Do you know how exhausted and hurt I am too? You don’t. You only care about yourself. You always say to me, “Little Leng, you don’t understand.” Fine. You understand everything. Since you understand so much, go be in a relationship all by yourself! Damn it, write back!!! An angry Leng 03 Lin, Will you please talk to me? I know I said terrible things last time. I regret them so much. Please, don’t ignore me. I’m scared. If you’re still angry, could you just send me “Get lost” or “Bastard”? At least let me know you’re doing all right aboard escort ship Alpha. Leng, who very much wants to hear from you 04 Lin, After all this time, I think I can finally accept the news that you’re gone. You really are something. Even colliding with an asteroid, you managed to keep the communications system intact. I still remember taking spacecraft piloting lessons together when we were young. I always found shortcuts, got a passing grade, and slipped off to play with you. But you were different: always so meticulous, making every detail perfect. I didn’t understand you then. I thought you were boring, as boring as those Chinese students in ancient times who insisted on full marks in every exam. But now I understand. Perfecting the details during practice gives you a greater margin for error in actual operations. Lately I’ve been looking through your operating manual from before your flight assessment. Your notes are so good, your handwriting so clear. I’ve learned a lot from them. Though your handwriting was still prettiest in your love letters to me, haha. I regret it so much. I should have kept all those letters with me. Now I can only turn through your notes to remember what we once had. Leng, missing you 05 Lin, I found a treasure last week. Haha, don’t be angry—not someone new. After all this flying, a small part of the oxygen system and food supply system you jettisoned hadn’t drifted away after all. Of course, thanks to your notes in the operating manual, a little maneuvering was all it took to put the escort ship on the path those systems would pass through. I didn’t take much: just an oxygen mask from your ship and your favorite apple milkshake. I wear the mask to sleep every day now. I think even your mask smells nicer than ours. I’ve been sleeping a little better, with fewer nightmares. I haven’t had the heart to drink the milkshake. I’m saving it for my birthday the month after next. Without you beside me, I don’t even want birthdays. Each one widens our age gap by another year. I’m old enough to be your aunt now, haha. If you were beside me, would you tug my ear again and say, “Asking for a beating, are you? Shameless thing.” I want you to tug my ear just one more time. Even in a dream. Leng, who found a treasure 06 Lin, I had a dream about you. I dreamed that while discussing the plan for the asteroid with me, you were stroking that model of combustible ice I had deliberately left aboard your ship. I also dreamed that when you told me to shut off the video link, your lips parted slightly and you said, “I love you. I’m sorry.” But why didn’t you tell me your real plan? Why didn’t you say a proper goodbye? I remember that at the end of the video, you told me to rest well, because things would be hard afterward. I didn’t take it seriously. Now I understand. Without your company, every minute, every second is hard to endure. Combustible ice is not incapable of burning. It is only trapped inside a cage of water molecules, just as I am trapped aboard this escort ship. Leng, both happy and sad to have dreamed of you 07 Lin, I’m full of regret today. If I’d studied harder back then, might I have found a better solution when the asteroid came toward us? I trusted you so much. I never doubted your plan, not even a little. You told me to cut the signal, and I cut it. You told me to lower the shield, and I lowered it. You told me to change direction and move onto the new orbit, and I did. At university, our teacher explained the binary-star model: two stars of similar mass share a common center of mass and can orbit one another very stably. I was so happy then, passing you a note: “Baby, are you my twin star?” I remember you taking it with a frown, then suddenly smiling around your brows when you unfolded it and saw what it said. You gave me a reproachful look, then pointed to the textbook, pretending to be stern. But clever as you are, how could you forget that this Prometheus Project of ours wasn’t a binary system at all? The mothership in the middle was so huge. All you had to do was get close to the asteroid and lock it together with escort ship Alpha. Aren’t you always so capable? You tamed me, unruly as I was. How could you not handle one menacing asteroid? A regretful Leng 08 Lin, We’ve flown beyond the Milky Way. Next month we’ll reach Andromeda. When we were little, you always said Andromeda was the best constellation because it was yours. Who would have thought humanity really would choose Andromeda as the site for the Prometheus Project? If you ask me, extinction is extinction. Even the Sun has a finite lifespan. What is so regrettable about a species having one too? You always call me “chaotic evil.” But do you know? I’m madly in love with your “lawful good,” with your restrained, stifled gasps in bed. Sometimes I truly hate the mothership, hate the Prometheus Project, and hate your meticulousness when you shoulder responsibility. Why must we always keep our promises? Even if the Prometheus Project fell apart, what could humanity far away in the Solar System do to us? Between the continuation of the human species and me, you chose the former. I never doubt your love for me, but I am sad. Why must you shoulder destiny? Why can’t you escape with me? Why can’t we let humanity’s story end with a love story? A heartbroken Leng 09 Lin, Sometimes I think I’m quite foolish too. Only after so long have I understood: it wasn’t that you didn’t understand binary systems. You weren’t willing to take even the slightest risk. By jettisoning the oxygen equipment and food supply system, you left yourself no way back. What, were you afraid I would fly toward you regardless of everything, as I did during that flight lesson when you had an accident? I regret it a little. I shouldn’t have let you know how well I could pilot. Then you wouldn’t have chosen to abandon all hope of survival just to stop me risking myself to rescue you. Perhaps it wasn’t entirely for me, either. After all, under those conditions, the two escort ships had little chance of docking successfully. And if we failed, the mothership carrying humanity’s last spark would have no protection left. Leng, with complicated feelings 10 Lin, The mothership has finally reached its intended destination. I’ve set up the program to send its location automatically. Once it lands on the new planet, we’ll be a true binary-star system. For humanity’s future, I’ve done everything I possibly can. I don’t know if you’re satisfied, but I really have used up all my strength. I grew the roses from seeds I smuggled aboard the escort ship. I also took apart your oxygen mask to make a flowerpot. Too many of my tears have stained it, and it’s a little rusty. But used to grow roses, it has a kind of vintage beauty. My original plan was to walk toward you with roses in my hands and propose once the mothership landed. Under Andromeda’s new sun, in the name of the starry sky, swearing by the earth, letting humanity’s future witness our love. Sadly, you didn’t give me that chance. But it’s all right, Lin. We don’t have to be twin stars. Since you can’t fly toward me, let me fly toward you. Lin, I’m coming. Leng, who loves you **Easter Eggs** 1. Lin and Leng are the only two escorts on humanity’s Prometheus Project. The project transports human genes to Andromeda aboard a mothership to prevent humanity’s extinction during the Sun’s transition into a white dwarf. 2. Lin comes from the name of the person I liked. Her name has many beautiful stories. Here I used one of them, taking Master Hejing’s surname as the protagonist’s name. 3. Leng comes from the literary allusion behind my own name: I took another character immediately beside it in the verse as the other protagonist’s name. 4. After her lover’s death, the fictional letter writer experiences the Five Stages of Grief. This plot follows the Kübler-Ross model, proposed by Elisabeth Kübler-Ross in her 1969 book *On Death and Dying*: denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance. 5. The title, *The Flowers Never Given*, uses roses for the bouquet as a tribute to the author’s favorite book, *The Little Prince*: “It is the time you have spent on your rose that makes your rose so precious.” 6. The illustration is Galaxy M81 from NASA’s “What Did Hubble See on Your Birthday?” series: The arms of the "grand design" spiral galaxy M81 are filled with young, bluish, hot stars. The greenish regions in the image are bright, gaseous clouds where new stars are forming. It also suggests humanity leaving the Solar System and arriving in a young, new stellar system. 7. This story was a birthday gift for someone I liked, so the illustration shows the sky seen by NASA’s Hubble telescope on her birthday.
